A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 21-page CritiQ paper, including Appendices A–F. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical body content, equations, tables, figures, and appendices; differences concern the first-page arXiv stamp and PDF metadata.

before.justification: v1 reports original human-preference agreement experiments, continual-pretraining evaluations, and ablations across code, math, and logic (Tables 1, 3, and 4).

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including agreement accuracies, downstream model evaluations, and ablations (Tables 1, 3, and 4).

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical knowledge-base retrieval, criteria evolution, worker-agent voting, Bradley–Terry scorer training, and data-selection procedures.

E1.justification: Both use the same Stack v2 Python, OpenWebMath non-code, and Zyda-2 data, with identical code, mathematics, and logical-reasoning evaluation tasks in Section 4.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Vanilla, TextGrad, and the same four QuRating criteria. Table 3 retains the original model and uniformly sampled training-data comparisons; no comparator membership changes.

E3.justification: Table 2 split sizes, model choices, annotation controls, training budgets, sampling temperatures, and evaluation procedures in Section 4 and Appendix A are identical.

E4.justification: The knowledge-base and evolution ablations, majority-voting comparison, criteria-distribution analysis, and refinement examples remain unchanged (Tables 1 and 4, Figure 3, and Appendix F).

E5.justification: Table 1 in both versions reports averages over five experiments with different random seeds. Run information and statistical reporting are unchanged throughout.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match. For example, Table 1 retains average accuracies of 87.32 for CritiQ Flow and 90.04 for CritiQ Scorer; downstream and ablation results also remain identical.

T1.justification: The judgment and accuracy definitions, scorer loss, sampling equations, and mathematical reasoning in Section 3 are identical. No assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about mining criteria from approximately 30 annotated pairs, efficient data selection, and improved downstream performance.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and applicability discussions are identical, including overfitting concerns and the stated limitations concerning three-domain coverage, human annotation biases, and constrained continual-pretraining experiments.

D1.justification: Hyperparameters and hardware in Appendix A, annotation instructions in Appendix B, prompts in Appendices C/E, and code/data access disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations, and the reference list are identical. Positioning relative to heuristic filtering, LLM quality assessment, QuRating, and reflection-based methods does not change.

P1.justification: Only the first-page margin stamp changes from v1 dated 26 Feb 2025 to v2 dated 7 Jul 2025. Title, authors, prose, headings, and document structure remain identical.

P2.justification: The updated first-page arXiv stamp is slightly repositioned. Figures 1–3, Tables 1–5, appendix boxes, captions, and all other page layouts are visually identical.

improvement.justification: The method, experiments, results, explanations, and appendices are unchanged. The version/date stamp and metadata updates have no meaningful effect on clarity, evidential support, or reproducibility.
